title: Clayface Gives Skydance Its Second Box Office Weekend Win In A Row

description: Clayface held off You Can See Everything to top the box office this weekend

title: Overwatch Co-Creator Pushes The Legend of California's Early Access Release To 2027
creator: Tomas Franzese
description: Jeff Kaplan's The Legend of California has shifted its early access launch from 2026 to 2027
contentEncoded: Former Overwatch developers Jeff Kaplan and Tim Ford are currently working on a survival game called The Legend of California at their new studio Kintsugiyama. While the game was previously slated for a Steam Early Access release in 2026, a new r/pcgaming Reddit AMA affirmed it has been pushed back to 2027.

title: The Most Broken D&D Item Keeps Ruining Games. Here Are 3 Ways to Fix It
creator: Francesco Cacciatore
description: One of the most common magic items in D&D is way overpowered for its cost, but here are three easy ways to fix it.
contentEncoded: Magic items are an important component of the Dungeons & Dragons experience; collecting and using wondrous artifacts is a given in a role-playing game of heroic fantasy. This is why, in D&D, every character class has access to magic items, starting at the very first level. However, one of these items is so powerful that it can easily turn the game’s balance upside down.

title: GTA: San Andreas’ Most Frustrating MIssion Show How Far Rockstar Has Come in 22 Years
creator: Paulo Kawanishi
categories: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas – The Definitive Edition
description: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is a classic game with interesting missions, but its annoying controls just feel worse after 22 years.
contentEncoded: With the imminent release of Grand Theft Auto 6, I decided it was time to revisit what was probably the biggest game of my childhood: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. In 2005, GTA: San Andreas was one of the first four games I bought for the PlayStation 2, alongside Final Fantasy X, Kingdom Hearts, and Devil May Cry 3. Since I can no longer enjoy that version of the game I played so many times as a kid, I picked up the Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy — Definitive Edition, which includes San Andreas, on Steam and booted up the game.
reason: Nostalgia retrospective about old game from 22 years ago

title: Nintendo Legend Reveals Super Mario Bros.' Most Surprising Innovation
creator: Patricia Hernandez
description: Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto pinpoints the NES game's most notable invention, which remains unique 41 years after the original Super Mario Bros.
contentEncoded: The original side-scrolling Super Mario Bros. is widely considered to be one of the best games of all time, and the list of reasons justifying that assertion is long. The NES game made Nintendo into a household name, and Mario into a media icon as recognizable as Mickey Mouse. The 1985 video game helped bring games into the mainstream, and it defined platforming as a video game genre. Super Mario Bros. remains one of the best-selling games of all time. Yet if you ask series creator Shigeru Miyamoto, none of these things truly capture SMB's biggest contribution to the world of video games.
reason: Video game news and analysis about Super Mario Bros. innovation.

title: BioWare's Closure Is Just the Tip of the Iceberg
creator: Oli Welsh
description: The Mass Effect and Dragon Age studio being shuttered by EA is a sign of a slow-motion industry crash that hasn't peaked
contentEncoded: We're in the middle of an outpouring of mourning for the studio, and for the Mass Effect Universe we never got. BioWare's talented developers will hopefully all go on to great things elsewhere, and many already have. (Who's looking forward to Exodus?) Maybe Mass Effect and Dragon Age will return; in this age of zombie IP, it seems a safe bet that they will. What's really lost at a moment like this, though, is institutional knowledge and culture, the malleable but enduring practices and principles that survive the departure of founders and team leads and are nurtured by new hands. It's a terrible loss.
reason: Video game industry news about BioWare studio closure by EA.

title: 9 Near-Perfect 'Far Side' Comics Starring the Nerdy Kid
creator: Brian VanHooker
description: Gary Larson's The Far Side didn't really have recurring characters, though some faces did appear more than once, like the Nerdy Kid
contentEncoded: One of the biggest differences between The Far Side and most other comic strips is that The Far Side doesn’t have a recurring cast of characters. Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, for example, had Charlie Brown, Linus, Lucy, Snoopy, and the rest of the gang, while Jim Davis’ Garfield has Garfield, Odie, Jon, and a handful of other recurring characters. But Gary Larson’s The Far Side, with its non-sequitur, single-panel jokes, didn’t have regular characters, or at least not really.
reason: Comic retrospective, not games or Steven's stated interests.

title: 5 Near-Perfect Psychological Thriller Movies Streaming for Free
creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
description: These tense genre picks are well worth your time.
contentEncoded: Psychological thrillers trigger a fight-or-flight response within a controlled environment and entertain us at the same time. Interpersonal relationships become the source of anxiety, as there’s more at stake than someone’s physical safety — their very sanity is on the line. The novelty of great psychological thrillers like Rear Window (1954), Memento (2000), or Mulholland Drive (2001) does not wear off after a first watch. There’s more to glean than suspense or twist, as catharsis is an integral part of the experience. Unfortunately, all those movies are locked up behind various streaming service subscriptions (if they're available to stream at all).

title: 23 Years Later, Spike's Best 'Buffy' Quote Is Still One of the Best Lines in TV History
creator: Jake Kleinman
description: Spike's best quote sums up his arc as one of the main characters in Buffy the Vampire Slayer.
contentEncoded: Buffy’s writers gave Spike some of the show’s sharpest one-liners — who could forget “Out. For. A. Walk. Bitch.”? But his best line comes in the series finale, “Chosen.” It’s the natural culmination of a character pulled between heroism and selfishness for most of his life, and it captures the complicated truth of his relationship with Buffy.

title: 61 Years Later, Paul's Best Dune Line Is Still the Coldest Quote in Sci-Fi History
creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
description: This brilliant quote from Frank Herbert's Dune reveals an unsavory truth.
contentEncoded: That said, the phenomenal success of Denis Villeneuve’s Dune movies proves that the impossible is always within reach. So far, Villeneuve’s adaptation has captured the sheer scale of the books and also made some meaningful changes to the source material. This version of Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) begins his journey with a hesitant vulnerability that feels more intense than in the books. This is also why his turn as a self-proclaimed messiah feels more ominous and devastating in Dune: Part Two.
